mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions and reduced corporate investment demand.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no statistically significant negative returns occur when the trigger is met (t-test p > 0.05), or the 20-day returns remain flat despite the rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) above the prior month's level coincides with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive triggered months, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05), or the negative return reverses direction within 2 days after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) by at least 5% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals a recovery in consumer confidence and economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous_month and HOUST > previous_to_previous_month by at least 5%
failure_condition: Across 100 such events, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect persists only for the first month and fades in the second month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month coincides with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects weak manufacturing momentum and reduced investment.
failure_condition: Over 10 such contractions, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when other demand proxies (e.g., GDPC1) are also contracting.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to immediate inflationary fears and preemptive rate hike anticipation.
failure_condition: In 50 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when other inflation indicators (e.g., core CPI) show no movement.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in unemployment and a rise in job openings (implied by UNRATE falling while not directly observable in the provided proxies) is expected to produce a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as labor market tightness improves.
failure_condition: When UNRATE declines but other labor proxies (PAYEMS) do not show significant hiring acceleration, or the 5-day forward returns remain flat (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A large monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; proxy via GDPC1 as a demand proxy) of at least 8% followed by a sustained 2-month period of high industrial supply (RSAFS > 700B), predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as both demand and supply improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous_month + 8% AND RSAFS > 700B for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 30 such events, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when the demand proxy (GDPC1) does not exceed the 8% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL < 305 for three consecutive months) in a deflationary regime is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate lower inflation and potential rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 305 for three consecutive months AND regime_hint='deflationary cycle'
failure_condition: In 20 such deflationary triplets, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when other macro indicators (e.g., FEDFUNDS) show tightening.
